content:
Today (17th), a netizen uploaded a clip on social media showing a suspected CCTV footage from a back alley, where three people were chatting on site, and at least two people were clearly seen wearing the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) uniform. According to the FEHD uniform information, the two were suspected to be a Hawker Control Officer and a Senior Hawker Control Officer.

The footage shows two officer-grade personnel chatting in the back alley. One of them first took out a cigarette and was smoking. Then, another Senior Hawker Control Officer walked over, took out a cigarette pack and a lighter, flicked his hair lightly, put a cigarette into his mouth, and left with his back to the camera, with a wisp of smoke emanating from his side.

Jizhik Society (集誌社) made an enquiry to the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department as to whether the people in the clip were FEHD staff. The department confirmed in its reply to the enquiry that the people in the clip were personnel of the FEHD's district hawker control team. A spokesperson said the incident took place in early June this year. The reporter asked whether FEHD personnel are allowed to smoke while wearing their uniforms? If the clip is true, have the personnel violated any rules? Will this affect the department's image? The FEHD replied that according to the department's established regulations, personnel are prohibited from smoking while wearing their uniforms and in public places.

The FEHD said that the department attaches great importance to the discipline and professional conduct of its staff, and has initiated a disciplinary investigation into the incident, and will take appropriate action in accordance with the established procedures and investigation results. The spokesperson also said that the department has clear requirements on the behaviour of personnel while wearing their uniforms, and any behaviour that violates the department's disciplinary requirements will be followed up seriously.
